name: L-Cysteine
aliases: E920, INS 920, L-cysteine, L cysteine, cysteine, L-cysteine hydrochloride
what_is: An amino acid used as a flour-treatment agent and for other technological purposes. Commercial L-cysteine can be produced by different manufacturing routes and sources.
why_botia: BOTIA flags E920 because the explicit additive name can matter both technologically and for source-sensitive dietary choices. The ingredient list can identify L-cysteine, but it normally cannot establish whether it was produced by fermentation, synthesis or from an animal-derived raw material.
can_1: Detect E920, L-cysteine and closely related declared names.
can_2: Show the texture/E-number context and explain that source may matter without labelling a generic E920 declaration as animal-derived.
cannot_1: Determine the manufacturing route or biological source from the generic name alone.
cannot_2: Certify vegetarian, vegan, halal or other source-dependent suitability without source information.
